youtube.title: Two Girls Photographed Fairies (True Story) 🧚
youtube.description:
In 1917, in Cottingley near Bradford, 16-year-old Elsie Wright and her 9-year-old cousin Frances Griffiths borrowed Elsie's father's camera and came back from the stream with a photo of Frances surrounded by dancing fairies. Her father didn't believe it, but a photographic expert found no sign of faking, and Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, the creator of Sherlock Holmes, published the photos in The Strand Magazine at Christmas 1920 as evidence of fairies, and later wrote a book about them.

People argued about the Cottingley Fairies for more than sixty years. In 1983 the cousins finally admitted the fairies were paper cutouts, copied from a children's book and held up with hatpins. But Frances insisted until her death that the fifth photograph was genuine.
